Distance Intersection over Union (LD -IoU) localization loss integrated 
into the YOLOv8 framework. B y incorporating the Lorentzian distance into the conventional IoU formulation, the 
proposed loss provides a more robust representation of spatial discrepancy, enabling more accurate bounding -box 
regression. Experiments conducted on the OAI dataset demonstr ate that the proposed framework consistently 
outperforms the baseline YOLOv8 and existing IoU -based localization losses. The proposed LD -IoU-YOLOv8 
achieved 99.1% precision, 94.2% mAP@0.5:0.95, 99.6% mAP@0.5, and 98.8% recall, while reducing the Box Loss 
from 0.291 to 0.093, corresponding to an approximately 68% relative reduction. Furthermore, the proposed localization 
loss demonstrated faster convergence than the conventional IoU loss, achieving high mAP@0.5 in fewer training 
epochs and providing more eff icient

The suggested LD -IoU-YOLOv8 algorithm was 
developed through the ap plication of the Ultralytics 
YOLOv8 library, which was based on the PyTorch 
deep learning framework. In order to make a 
comparison unbiased, the baseline YOLOv8 and the 
LD-IoU-YOLOv8 models were trained in equal 
experimental settings. The only difference between 
the models was their loss functions concerning 
localization, while all other aspects were the same. 
OAI Dataset was initially annotated through 
Roboflow platform, and it was subsequently 
preprocessed by resizing all knee X -ray images into 
640 × 640 pixels before training the model. While 
training the model, same value of batch size, learning 
rate, optimizer, and training epochs were used for 
both models in order to prevent any effect from 
training parameters on the result. The detection 
accuracy was calculated by the metrics. The complete

localization loss functions 
In order to test the efficacy of the proposed LD -
IoU loss, some more experiments were done using 
the localization loss function of YOLOv8 with other 
popular IoU loss functions. In addition to the 
conventional IoU, GIoU, DIoU, CIoU, and SIoU 
losses, three r ecent IoU -based localization losses, 
namely EIoU, WIoU, and Shape -IoU, were also 
included in the comparison to provide a more 
comprehensive evaluation against recent localization 
methods. All localization loss functions were 
implemented within the same YOL Ov8 architecture 
and evaluated under identical experimental 
conditions, including the same OAI dataset, data split, 
image preprocessing, optimizer, training schedule 
(100 epochs), hyperparameters, and evaluation 
protocol, ensuring a fair head -to-head compa rison. 
All experiments were done using the same OAI 
dataset, network

evidence.excerpt:
IoU across object detection architectures 
Further inve stigations on the generalization 
ability of the proposed LD-IoU localization loss were 
conducted by adopting the loss function in 
representative one -stage and two -stage object 
detection architectures and replacing their existing 
IoU losses. To ensure a fai r and reproducible 
comparison, all evaluated detectors were trained 
under identical experimental conditions. Specifically, 
all YOLO -based detectors employed the Medium 
(M) model architecture (YOLOv5m, YOLOv7, 
YOLOv8m, YOLOv9m, YOLOv10m, and 
YOLOv11m), while the Cascade R -CNN, Mask R -
CNN, and Faster R -CNN detectors were 
implemented using the standard ResNet -50-FPN 
backbone.  
 
 
 
Figure. 10 Epoch-wise convergence comparison of different localization loss functions during the 100 -epoch training 
process

evaluation_independence.corroboration_summary: Held-out test metrics, patient-level split evaluation, multi-seed runs, and an external Digital Knee X-ray dataset corroborate the reported gains.
evaluation_independence.final_evaluation_signal: Headline outcomes are reported using standard precision, recall, mAP@0.5, and mAP@0.5:0.95 metrics computed against ground-truth bounding boxes on held-out test splits.
evaluation_independence.optimization_signal: The bounding-box regression objective is trained using the proposed LD-IoU loss, which combines IoU with normalized Lorentzian center distance.

primary.claim_evidence_alignment: Claims regarding superior bounding box regression, lower box loss, faster convergence, and cross-model applicability are well substantiated by tabular results, training loss curves, and external testing.
primary.evaluation_assessment: The evaluation includes extensive controlled comparisons against eight existing IoU-based losses (IoU, GIoU, DIoU, CIoU, SIoU, EIoU, WIoU, and Shape-IoU) under identical experimental setups, multi-seed statistical significance analysis with Student's t-distribution confidence intervals, cross-architecture generalization across six YOLO variants and three two-stage detectors, ablation of raw versus normalized formulation, patient-level split validation to test for data leakage, and external dataset testing.

evaluation_independence.corroboration_summary: Standard mAP and classification metrics against ground truth labels on held-out test splits, patient-level splits, and an independent external Digital Knee X-ray dataset corroborate the performance improvements.
evaluation_independence.final_evaluation_signal: Standard object detection benchmark metrics including precision, recall, mAP@0.5, and mAP@0.5:0.95 calculated against ground-truth bounding boxes and Kellgren-Lawrence grade annotations.
evaluation_independence.optimization_signal: Training loss combining classification loss, distribution focal loss, and bounding-box regression guided by the proposed LD-IoU loss (or baseline IoU variants).

primary.limitations: The authors acknowledge limitations including primary validation on single-modality X-ray datasets from OAI, the need for evaluation on larger patient-independent cohorts across multi-center clinical settings, and testing on other imaging modalities such as MRI or CT.
primary.method_assessment: The formulation of LD-IoU is clearly defined mathematically, demonstrating how the raw Lorentzian distance is normalized using the smallest enclosing box dimensions to achieve scale invariance. The architecture modifications and integration into YOLOv8 are explicitly documented without requiring changes to backbone parameters or distribution focal loss.
primary.quality_rationale: The study presents a clear, well-scoped methodological advancement with transparent loss function equations and rigorous empirical validation. The experimental protocol ensures proper baselines with fixed hyperparameters, addresses potential leakage via patient-level splits, and verifies generalizability across multiple detector architectures and an external dataset.
primary.scoped_contribution: The paper introduces LD-IoU, a bounding-box regression loss incorporating normalized Lorentzian distance between bounding box centers alongside standard intersection over union to improve localization accuracy and convergence speed in YOLOv8 and other object detection frameworks applied to knee osteoarthritis detection.

scholarly_quality.rationale: The study presents a clear, well-scoped methodological advancement with transparent loss function equations and rigorous empirical validation. The experimental protocol ensures proper baselines with fixed hyperparameters, addresses potential leakage via patient-level splits, and verifies generalizability across multiple detector architectures and an external dataset.
scholarly_quality.uncertainty: The authors acknowledge limitations including primary validation on single-modality X-ray datasets from OAI, the need for evaluation on larger patient-independent cohorts across multi-center clinical settings, and testing on other imaging modalities such as MRI or CT.
